newsitem.title: CHINA: China to halt some U.S. textile, farm imports. [CORRECTED 10:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: China to halt some U.S. textile, farm imports. [CORRECTED 10:25 GMT]

text.p: China said on Sunday it planned to suspend temporarily its imports of some U.S. textiles, farm goods and alcoholic drinks in retaliation for U.S. curbs on its textile goods.
The temporary ban would take effect on December 10 (corrects from December 6) and follows what Beijing calls severe violations of a bilateral textile accord by the United States.
"The decision was made in response to the U.S. unilateral cut of import quotas of Chinese textiles, which severely violated the bilateral textile agreement," the official Xinhua news agency said.
In September, Washington announced punitive charges against import quotas for Chinese textile goods, accusing China of using transshipments to avoid U.S. quota restrictions.
The action -- which was expected to cost China about $19 million -- marked the first time Washington had imposed so-called triple charges against repeated violations of a bilateral textile accord.

"On September 6, the U.S. Trade Representative Office levied charges against China's 1996 textile quotas of 195,000 dozens and 134,000 kilogrammes of items covering 13 categories, and invoked triple charges on five of the categories for the first time," Xinhua said.
The action was made without full consultation and clear supporting evidence, the news agency added.
Beijing accused Washington of imposing a series of barriers that had seriously affected Chinese textile export to the U.S. as well as China's ability to pay for American imports.
China said it had urged the U.S. to withdraw its decision but its pleas had been ignored, leaving it with no choice but to take action.
It did not indicate which products would be included under the broad import categories set for import suspensions.
But Xinhua said the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation and the General Administration of Customs would have a detailed list ready before December 10.
China said it opposed any attempt to impose the will of one side upon others in trade matters and called on the U.S. to avoid such measures in future.

"Once again, we wish to urge the United States to handle trade disputes in the spirit of advancing bilateral trade, and refrain from taking any actions harmful to bilateral trade in the future," it said.
